To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the early osteoblast progenitor population in murine bone marrow is contained within the CD45R−/low CD11b− CD115high fraction, and that osteoclast progenitors are contained within the CD3− CD11b−low CD115high fraction.
the early osteogenic activity in total mouse BM is recapitulated by the CD11b-CD45R-CD3-CD115high population, which contains the early osteoclastic progenitor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of bone marrow-derived stem cell-based therapies to regenerate the bone marrow and the immune system.
the identification and characterization of osteoclast precursor populations and the factors that regulate their differentiation.
the development of new methods of analysis of the bone microstructure and the development of new bone tissue substitutes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the osteoclast progenitors in murine bone marrow are heterogeneous and are contained in at least four distinct populations.

the osteoclast progenitors are a heterogeneous population of cells that can be divided into two major groups: (1) the CD11bhighCD45R−CD115high cells that express the osteoclast-specific transcription factor, NFATc1, and can differentiate into multinucleated cells in vitro in the absence of RANKL, and (2) the CD11bloCD45R− cells that express high levels of the osteoclastogenic transcription factor, PU.1,
the osteoclastogenic potential of the murine bone marrow is contained within a population of CD45R− CD115high cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a population of osteoclast progenitors in the CD11b-CD115+ fraction of murine bone marrow that are committed to the osteoclast lineage.
there are multiple osteoclast progenitors in murine BM, and that they are not all contained within the CD115high population.
we have identified multiple osteoclast progenitors that can give rise to osteoclasts in the murine BM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
osteoclasts are derived from multiple precursor populations in the BM, which may be differentially regulated by environmental factors.
there are at least three distinct populations of osteoclast precursor cells in murine BM.
the early osteogenic activity of total BM is contained within this fraction of cells, which we have termed “osteoclast precursor cells” (OPCs).
